analysis.investment_thesis: Aether Industries' Magic Formula scores are disqualifying: Earnings Yield of ~1.5% (EBIT INR 241 Cr / EV ~INR 15,850 Cr) is roughly 10x below my 15% threshold, and ROIC of ~9.6% (EBIT / invested capital of ~INR 2,512 Cr) falls well short of the 20% hurdle. The market is paying a decade's worth of growth upfront — that removes the margin of safety the formula requires.
key_strengths: High operating margins (29%) suggest real pricing power in specialty chemicals niche
Near-debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.09) with strong promoter backing (74.9%)
Revenue and EBITDA recovering sharply in FY2025 (EBITDA INR 279 Cr, +63% YoY) after FY2024 dip
key_risks: Earnings Yield of ~1.5% is catastrophically low — Magic Formula demands >12%; current valuation bakes in perfection
Free cash flow has been deeply negative all 4 years (-INR 157 to -452 Cr) as capex exceeds all earnings; CWIP of INR 556 Cr signals more capex ahead
ROE of only 7.8% reveals massive equity dilution (reserves jumped from INR 274 Cr to INR 2,196 Cr in 3 years) suppressing returns on the swollen capital base
red_flags: Earnings Yield ~1.5% — worst possible score on Magic Formula metric #1
ROIC ~9.6% — below my 12% minimum threshold; ROE 7.8% confirms poor capital returns
OCF positive in only 1 of last 4 years; cumulative FCF burn ~INR 1,316 Cr while the business generated ~INR 479 Cr net profit over same period
P/E 70x, EV/EBITDA 46x — market is pricing future perfection, not current fundamentals
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running Aether through the Magic Formula: EV ≈ INR 15,850 Cr (market cap INR 15,667 Cr + debt INR 200 Cr − cash INR 17 Cr). EBIT (operating income) FY2025 = INR 241 Cr. Earnings Yield = 241/15,850 = 1.52% — one of the worst scores possible; my formula demands >15%. Invested capital ≈ equity INR 2,329 Cr + debt INR 200 Cr − cash INR 17 Cr = INR 2,512 Cr, giving ROIC = 241/2,512 = 9.6%, confirmed by the reported ROCE of 10.2%. Both pillars of the Magic Formula fail badly. This is a business the market loves at a price I cannot justify systematically.

The underlying business has genuine qualities — 29% operating margins, a defensible specialty chemicals niche, and an FY2025 EBITDA rebound to INR 279 Cr after the FY2024 dip to INR 171 Cr. But the company is in a multi-year capital-intensive buildout phase: INR 452 Cr of capex in FY2025 alone against INR 100 Cr of operating cash flow leaves FCF at −INR 352 Cr. CWIP of INR 556 Cr signals this cash burn continues. The equity base has ballooned 6x in 3 years (IPO proceeds), compressing ROE to 7.8% — good businesses earning 7.8% ROE on a 70x P/E multiple are not Magic Formula candidates. If ROIC normalizes to 20%+ and capacity comes online, the story may change. At current prices, pass.
